articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Potential Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs Trades After Colts' Nelson, Buckner Deals
articles.summary: Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs have emerged as names that could be on the trade block amid the Indianapolis Colts' on-the-fly rebuild.
articles.body:
Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs have emerged as names that could be on the trade block amid the Indianapolis Colts' on-the-fly rebuild.

On the heels of the 2-5 Colts dealing guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers on Tuesday, there is some belief that they may not be done selling off pieces.

The biggest trade asset remaining on Indy's roster is Taylor, although there is reportedly some doubt over whether interim general manager Ed Dodds would be willing to move him.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , opposing teams "aren't totally sold" on the Colts trading Taylor "despite heavy interest." He added that Taylor "isn't a slam dunk" to get moved.

The Colts signed Taylor to a two-year, $44 million contract extension in August, meaning he is under contract through 2028.

ESPN's Dan Graziano noted that Taylor's contract is "tradeable" since the acquiring team would only have to take on $8 million in prorated salary plus bonus money for this season, and could technically move on from Taylor within five days after the Super Bowl without having to make any financial commitment for next season.

While the Colts do appear to be in the midst of a fire sale, it is fair to wonder if they would trade Taylor since he is the face of the franchise, signed for multiple years and the centerpiece of the offense, having eclipsed 1,400 rushing yards in each of the past two seasons.

As for Downs, he is set to become a free agent during the offseason, perhaps making him more attainable.

Per Fowler, Downs "has emerged as a hot name this week" since multiple teams with a need at wide receiver have "shown interest" in him.

Fowler added that he senses Downs "would not be against a change of scenery," although he isn't sure if the Colts will move them since they are already thin at wide receiver with Alec Pierce on injured reserve.

A third-round pick by the Colts in the 2023 NFL draft, Downs set career highs in 2024 with 72 receptions for 803 yards and five touchdowns, but his production dipped last season to 58 grabs for 566 yards and four touchdowns.

He is on pace for a career-worst season in 2026, recording 26 catches for 307 yards and no touchdowns through seven games.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Brian Thomas Jr., Chances of Jaguars Dealing WR Before 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Now that trade deadline season is in full swing after the Indianapolis Colts' moves on Tuesday, another AFC South team appears poised to make a significant deal within the next two weeks.
articles.body:
Now that trade deadline season is in full swing after the Indianapolis Colts' moves on Tuesday, another AFC South team appears poised to make a significant deal within the next two weeks.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the feeling among multiple executives around the NFL is that Brian Thomas Jr.'s days with the Jacksonville Jaguars "are numbered" as his role in the offense has significantly diminished this season.

In the same article, Dan Graziano noted several teams still consider Thomas to be a "high-end talent" and would trade "something of value" to bring him in.

Fowler did add it's not considered a "slam dunk" that Thomas will get moved, but a fresh start could serve the third-year wideout well.

The Jaguars are in a tricky spot because they would seemingly not want to trade Thomas within the AFC given that they are a strong playoff contender and don't want the risk of him potentially helping a team they could go up against in January.

Teams like the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers have been cited as potentially searching for receiver help leading up to the trade deadline.

Another potential hurdle could be the cost if the Jaguars are using the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade as a comparison. The Arizona Cardinals were able to get a 2027 second-round draft pick from the Houston Texans for Harrison.

It's not an unfair comparison since both players recently turned 24 and were first-round picks in the 2024 draft. Thomas' ceiling in the NFL is much higher than Harrison's since he put up 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie.

So far this season, it does seem like Thomas isn't a factor in Jacksonville's offensive game plan. He has nine catches in six games, has played fewer than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in three of those contests, including a total of 15 snaps in Week 6 against the Texans.

This does feel like the last opportunity for the Jaguars to get any significant value for Thomas. An acquiring team would be getting him at a time when they can evaluate his play with his fifth-year option needing to be decided on in the offseason.

The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10. Jacksonville has two games in a four-day span starting on Sunday against the Colts before a Week 9 Thursday night matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on Nov. 5.

articles.title: Justin Tucker, Chiefs Reportedly Agree to Contract Amid Harrison Butker's Struggles
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are reportedly bringing in veteran competition for struggling kicker Harrison Butker.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are reportedly bringing in veteran competition for struggling kicker Harrison Butker.

According to Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, the Chiefs are signing veteran kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad.

The move comes amid Butker converting just 11 of his 16 field goal attempts (68.8 percent) through six games this season.

Tucker, 36, spent 13 seasons with the Baltimore Ravens from 2012 to 2024, establishing himself as one of the most successful kickers in NFL history during that time.

A seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro, one-time Super Bowl champion and member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame's All-Decade Team for the 2010s, Tucker was a consistent performer for most of his tenure in Baltimore.

Among qualified players, he is the second-most-accurate kicker in NFL history, making 89.1 percent of his field goal attempts.

Tucker also ranks 14th in NFL history in total field goals made (417) and 17th in career points scored (1,775).

However, Tucker had the worst season of his career in 2024, which was when he kicked most recently in an NFL regular-season contest.

Tucker made a career-low 73.3 percent of his field goals that season, going 22-for-30. He also missed two of his 62 extra-point tries.

While Tucker has participated in tryouts and workouts with the New Orleans Saints, Indianapolis Colts and New York Jets since 2024, joining the Chiefs' practice squad marks the first time he has officially joined a new team since departing Baltimore.

Like Tucker, Butker has long been considered one of the top kickers of his generation, winning three Super Bowls during his 10-year run in Kansas City.

Butker is also among the most-accurate kickers in NFL history, ranking fifth on the all-time list with a field goal percentage of 87.3 percent.

He is trending toward performing below his career field goal percentage for the fourth time in the past five seasons, though, and his five missed field goals this season already match the amount he had all of last season.

Butker had an especially tough time during a 20-3 road loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night, missing two of his three field goal attempts.

Signing Tucker to the practice squad is not a guarantee that Butker will lose his job, but if the misses continue to pile up, the Chiefs now have an experienced secondary option they can turn to.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Titans' Tony Pollard Amid Jonathan Taylor Buzz at 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Amid the focus on marquee names such as Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley as potential trade candidates, Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard could be most prominent player at the position to get moved before Nov. 10.
articles.body:
Amid the focus on marquee names such as Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley as potential trade candidates, Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard could be most prominent player at the position to get moved before Nov. 10.

Per ESPN's Dan Graziano , Pollard is considered "more likely" to be traded than someone like Taylor.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler wrote in a separate report that Pollard is viewed as an "attractive fallback plan" if the Colts decide to hold on to Taylor.

Fowler did quote one AFC executive who was skeptical of the Titans moving Pollard because they don't think the team wants to "take weapons away" from Cam Ward right now.

One reason a Pollard deal would seem more likely than Taylor getting traded is contractual. Pollard is in the final season of his three-year, $21.8 million contract with Tennessee.

Taylor just signed a two-year, $44 million extension with the Indianapolis Colts in August. His 2027 salary of $16 million doesn't become fully guaranteed until February 19, so in theory a team could decide to move on from him without any long-term financial commitment.

However, given the Colts' reported asking price for Taylor is at least a second-round draft pick, an acquiring team would seem unlikely to give up that much for a rental back.

Pollard has been a bright spot in what has otherwise been a disappointing Titans offense. The 29-year-old ranks 10th in the NFL with 478 rushing yards and is tied for 11th with four rushing touchdowns.

He is also a reliable receiver out of the backfield with at least 30 catches in each of the past five seasons.

Given Pollard's age and contract status, it wouldn't seem to make much sense for the Titans to prioritize keeping him if they can get a decent mid-round draft pick back.

articles.title: NFL Exec Links Cowboys to Josh Sweat Trade at 2026 Deadline, 'Makes a Lot of Sense'
articles.summary: Some NFL teams are expecting the Arizona Cardinals to follow up their trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans by parting ways with edge rusher Josh Sweat, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
Some NFL teams are expecting the Arizona Cardinals to follow up their trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans by parting ways with edge rusher Josh Sweat, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.

According to Fowler, "rival teams could see [Sweat] getting moved" ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

One NFC executive told Fowler: "Sweat to Dallas makes a lot of sense to me. That's a profile fit."

Fowler noted there are rumors 29-year-old Sweat wants an extension despite already being signed through 2028, which "could complicate" a potential trade. He still named the Cowboys as well as the Chicago Bears and San Francisco 49ers as potential "team fits" for Sweat.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said in a Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan he felt it was "unlikely" the Cowboys' defense would get the opportunity to add a player from outside the organization this season, per DallasCowboys.com's Tommy Yarrish .

"But if it's there, I'll do it," Jones added, per Yarrish.

Discussion of the Cowboys' edge depth is taking place after the organization traded a 2027 fourth-round draft pick to the Green Bay Packers in order to acquire Rashan Gary over the offseason.

Cowboys just improved to 3-4 and upped their chances of winning the NFC East with a Monday night win over the Eagles, but Gary and the Dallas pass rush once more struggled to put pressure on a Philadelphia offense that recorded 200 yards through the air.

Sweat, who is in the second year of his four-year, $76.4 million deal with the Cardinals, has recorded two sacks, 16 tackles (three for loss) and four quarterback hits in seven games this season.

He has added 12 pressures, 10 stops and eight hurries, according to PFF , but popped up on the Cardinals injury report earlier this fall after undergoing an undisclosed procedure this offseason.

Sweat's health, the Cardinals' asking price and the Cowboys' willingness to further chip away at their limited 2027 draft stock in a push to win an injury-weakened division could determine how seriously Jones considers a potential trade.

Jones will get his next look at Sweat this Sunday, when the Cardinals (2-5) arrive in Dallas for a 1 p.m. ET Week 8 matchup.

articles.title: Chiefs reportedly sign Justin Tucker to practice squad after Harrison Butker misses two field goals in Week 7
articles.summary: Justin Tucker has not kicked in the NFL since 2024.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs could be on the verge of replacing longtime kicker Harrison Butker. Days after Butker missed two field goals in an embarrassing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, the Chiefs reportedly signed kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad, per the Kansas City Star.

Tucker has not appeared in the NFL since the 2024 season. He was released by the Baltimore Ravens ahead of the 2025 NFL season after being accused of sexual misconduct by multiple massage therapists.

Tucker has received tryouts with other NFL teams in the years since his release, but has gone unsigned until now.

Prior to his release, Tucker was considered one of the best kickers in the NFL. From 2013 to 2023, he made the All-Pro first team five times and was a seven-time Pro Bowler.

His performance, however, started to slip in his final season with the Ravens. Tucker made a career-worst 73.3% of his field-goal attempts that year, with many of his misses coming from longer distances. Despite that, it looked as though the Ravens planned to bring Tucker back in 2025 until accusations against him came to light.

Tucker was ultimately handed a 10-game suspension from the NFL ahead of the 2025 season. Though he was not with a team, the NFL counted the first 10 weeks of the regular season as time served for Tucker. Because of that, he will be eligible to kick immediately if the Chiefs promote him to their active roster.

Prior to 2026, Butker had been a model of consistency on the field. The 31-year-old was coming off a nine-year stretch in which he made at least 84% of his field goals in every season.

But Butker has experienced some uncharacteristic misses to start 2026. In addition to his two missed field goals against the Seahawks, Butker has missed three other field-goal attempts so far, the majority of which have come from 50+ yards out, where Butker has made just 2-of-6 attempts this year.

articles.title: New Jets Rumors on Aaron Glenn's Hot Seat as HC After Loss to Dolphins, 2-5 Start to 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn isn't in imminent danger of losing his job with the team sitting at 2-5, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn isn't in imminent danger of losing his job with the team sitting at 2-5, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler .

Graziano reported his sense is that Glenn will remain in the role for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season, after which ownership and the front office will make an evaluation.

Fowler wrote that "Glenn likely will get some time to attempt to right the ship, but the hot seat conversation is real."

The Jets are situated well with three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL draft. Few expected them to be a big winner this year, so from the outset, the season was about setting the table for the future.

According to Graziano, that's the basis on which Glenn will mostly be judged:

"What the Jets want to have established by the end of this season is at least a foundation of a winning culture and an environment in which a young quarterback would be in position to quickly thrive and be happy. It's hard to look at the Jets right now and think they're on either one of those tracks. There is time to turn it around, but if it keeps going the way it has so far, this is absolutely a situation we'll be watching for a potential change."

Fowler ended the conversation by saying it's unlikely the Jets would kick general manager Darren Mougey to the curb in the offseason since he has done well to build up their draft assets.

There are some encouraging signs from the team.

Braelon Allen has anchored the backfield with Breece Hall injured. He eclipsed the century mark for the second time in the 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins.

David Bailey is tied for fifth in the league in sacks with 5.5. Fellow rookies Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr. have shown flashes.

But New York has yet to win a game within the division under Glenn. By now, fans have probably seen the stat about how badly the team is getting outscored in the final two minutes as well.

There's arguably more evidence in favor of firing Glenn than retaining him, but a coaching change wouldn't achieve much. The Jets aren't a playoff-caliber team, and whoever succeeds Glenn would be an interim replacement rather than a coach who may guide the team in 2027 and beyond.

Maybe the situation continues to devolve to a point where Glenn absolutely has to go. Otherwise, giving him the rest of the season might be the best call.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Sounds Off on 'Frustrating' Offensive Showing in Chiefs' Loss to Seahawks
articles.summary: Travis Kelce is frustrated with the effort a shorthanded Kansas City Chiefs offense put in against the Seattle Seahawks while conceding the team's first loss of the season last Sunday.
articles.body:
Travis Kelce is frustrated with the effort a shorthanded Kansas City Chiefs offense put in against the Seattle Seahawks while conceding the team's first loss of the season last Sunday.

The Chiefs went without a trip to the red zone for the first time in the Patrick Mahomes era in the 20-3 Week 6 road defeat.

"It felt like they were playing prevent the entire time. It just let the front four cause havoc in the run game and get out of the pocket... It was a pretty frustrating game from the jump," Kelce told his brother Jason Kelce around the 30:00 mark of Wednesday's New Heights podcast .

Kelce continued, "It's frustrating, because we were rolling as a unit for a while there. And I think we're not far off from getting right back to it... I think we just need to learn from this, feel how it felt to get our tail kicked like that, and never let it happen again."

Kelce pointed toward the turning point of the loss taking place when he was called for an illegal motion penalty on the first drive.

"We were rolling, that first drive, and that just kind of stalled us," Kelce said. "From there, it was just bad techniques, bad fundamentals, just okay effort."

The Chiefs were missing injured wide receivers Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice from the loss, during which Mahomes completed just 57.6 percent of his passes and threw an interception.

Eight players including Kelce made a catch last Sunday, but the group combined for just 165 receiving yards and no touchdowns.

Kelce said the Chiefs' receiving unit, which will still be missing at least Thornton for Week 7 amid his recovery from the significant ankle injury he suffered earlier this month, will need to focus on working together in order to give Mahomes more opportunities for success going forward.

"If it's the backside of a route, being ready and on time. If it's the called route that we're trying to get open, being on time, and being where you need to be... making the read easy for Pat to get the ball out on time so that the offensive line doesn't have to strain for more than what they typically do," Kelce said.

The Chiefs (5-1) are still heading into Week 7 in the top spot of the AFC West, but that could change based on this weekend's matchup against the Denver Broncos (5-2).

Whether Mahomes, Kelce and the rest of the Chiefs offense are able to rebound from their blowout defeat by Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET in Denver could play a role in which team makes it out of the division this winter.

articles.title: How Justin Tucker’s 89.1% career accuracy compares with Harrison Butker’s career-low 68.8% this season
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs signed kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad on Wednesday, days after Harrison Butker missed two field goals in a loss at
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs signed kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad on Wednesday, days after Harrison Butker missed two field goals in a loss at Seattle. Butker has made 11 of 16 attempts this season, a career-low 68.8%. Tucker, 36, owns an 89.1% career rate, second best in NFL history, but he has not kicked in the league since 2024. The Chiefs are 5-1, and head coach Andy Reid has not handed the job to anyone else. Still, a seven-time Pro Bowler now stands a few yards away from the man he might replace.Justin Tucker's 89.1% career rate against Butker's 68.8% this seasonJustin Tucker's number comes from a long stretch of work. Across 13 seasons in Baltimore he led the league at 94.6% in 2021 and posted a career-best 97.4% in 2016. His 417 made field goals rank 14th all time. He also once held the NFL record with a 66-yarder against Detroit. That is what a team is buying when it wants certainty.Butker's 68.8% is a different kind of figure. It covers only six games, so one clean weekend could move it a lot. But the drop is steep. He made 86.8% in 2025 and 88.4% from 2017 through 2025. This year he sits almost 20 points below his own norm.Butker began the season third all time, behind Tucker and Cameron Dicker. Now he is working against his own record. The sample is small enough that a recovery is still possible, but the Chiefs have seen enough to buy some insurance.Seattle showed the problemSunday night made it plain. Butker missed a 58-yard field goal at the end of the first half and a 45-yarder in the fourth quarter. Kansas City lost 20-3, so every point mattered.A 58-yarder is a long try for anyone. The 45-yarder is the one that should bother the Chiefs. He has also missed an extra point this year, and NBC Sports counts seven misses across his last 11 games.Reid did not dodge it afterward. "He's been one of the most consistent kickers in football." He added that Butker is a bit off and has to fix it.Butker has three Super Bowl rings in Kansas City. That history buys patience.Why Justin Tucker is on the practice squadTucker is not on the 53-man roster, and Butker's job is not in immediate danger. The Chiefs are 5-1, which gives them room to wait. They worked out three kickers this week and picked Tucker over former Rams kicker Harrison Mevis.The résumé comes with questions. In 2024 Tucker went 22 of 30, or 73.3%, the worst season of his career. The NFL then suspended him for 10 games in 2025, and the Ravens released him in May of that year. Tucker has maintained that he did nothing inappropriate. Workouts followed with the Saints, Colts and Jets, but no contract.So the Chiefs are weighing a proven career against a rough last season and a long layoff. If Butker misses again, they will not have to start a search. Practice squad players can also be elevated for game days, so a switch would not take much paperwork.For now, Tucker practices and Butker kicks.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jonathan Taylor's Trade Stance Revealed by Colts' Shane Steichen After Nelson, Buckner Deals
articles.summary: In the aftermath of the Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner trades, Jonathan Taylor isn't trying to force his way off the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
In the aftermath of the Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner trades, Jonathan Taylor isn't trying to force his way off the Indianapolis Colts.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Wednesday that Taylor has not requested a trade at this point.

When asked if Nelson or Buckner made a trade request, Steichen opted to keep it in house.

"I'll keep all of that private," he said.

Coming off three straight losses and the decision to fir e general manager Chris Ballard after a Week 6 defeat against the Tennessee Titans, the Colts officially entered sell mode on Tuesday.

Indianapolis started the day by sending Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks for two draft picks, including a 2027 third-round selection. Buckner followed a few hours later when he was traded to the San Francisco 49ers for a fourth-round pick in 2027.

Taylor is the biggest name the Colts could potentially move, though it's unclear how much activity there has been around him to this point.

The Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Minnesota Vikings, and Denver Broncos have been cited as teams that could have interest, but there's no indication any of them have put together a formal offer.

Per ESPN's Jordan Raanan , some people in the NFL believe the Colts will seek a second-round pick "and possibly more" if they trade Taylor.

Indianapolis is in a difficult spot right now with a 2-5 record and not having a first-round pick in the 2027 draft because it was traded to the New York Jets last year in the Sauce Gardner deal.

Based on the current standings , the Colts will be sending the No. 7 overall pick to the Jets. Their trades of Nelson and Buckner have them with a total of nine projected selections in the draft.

A key difference for Taylor compared to Nelson and Buckner is contract status. Nelson and Buckner are in the final season of their current deals and over the age of 30.

Taylor has two more years remaining on his contract beyond this season after signing a two-year, $44 million extension in August. He is one of the few bright spots for a struggling Colts team right now.

The three-time Pro Bowler ranks fifth in the NFL in rushing yards (587) and is tied for the league lead in rushing touchdowns (eight).

Despite Taylor's individual success since entering the league, he hasn't made the playoffs with the Colts since his rookie year in 2020. They haven't finished over .500 since 2023 (9-8).

The NFL trade deadline isn at 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10 if the Colts want to make additional moves as they look toward the future amid a season that is quickly spiraling out of control.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes comparison puts Caleb Williams in the spotlight after Terrell Owens reacts to Bears QB’s rapid rise
articles.summary: Caleb Williams is giving the Chicago Bears a reason to believe their offense can compete with the NFL’s best, and Hall of Fame wide receiver Terrell Owens
articles.body: Caleb Williams is giving the Chicago Bears a reason to believe their offense can compete with the NFL’s best, and Hall of Fame wide receiver Terrell Owens has noticed. After back-to-back 300-yard passing performances, Williams has drawn a striking comparison to Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes. The timing matters. Williams missed three games with a hamstring injury, yet his return has brought fresh energy to Chicago’s playoff push. Owens believes the young quarterback is beginning to show why the Bears made him the No. 1 overall pick in 2024.Terrell Owens names Caleb Williams and Patrick Mahomes among NFL’s most dynamic QBsOwens shared his thoughts on Williams during his “Get TO The Point” podcast, praising the quarterback’s recent performances while making it clear that his playing ability matters far more than his personal style.“You already know. Number one. Paint my nail with this lip,” Owens said. “ This dude right here. Hey, Caleb, I paint my nails every weekend. Williams. The man, the Chicago Bears, these guys are balling. I don’t know what else to say about him. All I know is right now, he’s definitely special. This is his second week over 300 yards passing.“Painting nails or no painting nails, you cannot deny this guy’s ability and his talent. I think this is why they drafted him. I think at the end of last season, going into the playoffs, again, they should have gone further. Now you’re starting to see this guy really emerge. I think the game is starting to slow down.”Williams backed up that praise with a strong showing against the New England Patriots. He threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in Chicago’s 30-24 win, helping the Bears improve to 5-2. The performance followed an equally impressive display against Atlanta, where he completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions.Those outings made Williams the first Bears quarterback to throw for more than 300 yards in consecutive games since Mitch Trubisky did it in three straight games in 2018.Owens then took the comparison further, putting Williams alongside one of the league’s most accomplished quarterbacks.“When you talk about dynamic quarterbacks, between him and Patrick Mahomes, these are the two most dynamic quarterbacks at that position,” Owens added.Caleb Williams’ progress gives Chicago more reasons for optimismThe comparison is about Caleb Williams’ style and potential, not a claim that he has already reached Mahomes’ level of achievement. His ability to create plays when protection breaks down, move outside the pocket and deliver difficult throws has caught attention. Now, he is also showing better control of the offense.That development could matter more to Chicago than any individual statistic. Williams has sometimes relied on his natural talent to escape pressure and extend plays. His recent performances suggest he is becoming more comfortable making quick decisions and working within the offense.The Bears have won four of their last five games, and Williams’ return has strengthened their position as they chase a playoff spot. He has also credited his offensive line and receivers for helping him succeed, a sign that he understands how much the team's performance depends on everyone doing their job.Mahomes remains the benchmark for quarterbacks who can change a game with both planned plays and improvisation. Williams still has plenty to prove over a full season, but Owens’ comments reflect a growing sense that Chicago may finally be seeing its young quarterback put everything together.The next test comes against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8. Another strong performance would give Williams a chance to show that his recent surge is more than a brief hot streak.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Joe Burrow, Ryan Rehkow earn NFL weekly awards
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow and punter Ryan Rehkow earned AFC weekly awards after the Week 7 win over the Baltimore Ravens.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow and punter Ryan Rehkow earned AFC weekly awards after the Week 7 win over the Baltimore Ravens .

articles.title: Browns rumors: Cleveland’s 5-2 record puts them on ‘low-key’ trade deadline bombshell watch
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have been one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 season. Cleveland is 5-2 heading into Week 8 and sits atop the AFC North division sta...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have been one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 season. Cleveland is 5-2 heading into Week 8 and sits atop the AFC North division standings alongside Pittsburgh. This shocking turn of events could impact how the Browns approach the upcoming NFL trade deadline .

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano shared intel from around the league in their latest article. They touched on how Cleveland could actually become buyers at the deadline after their hot start.

"Cleveland is a low-key team to watch at the deadline. The Browns are 5-2 and like to make deals," Fowler wrote. "Defensive line help will be available if they tap into it. And adding a versatile blocker, either at tight end or H-back, would be timely, perhaps providing a player similar to what Todd Monken had in Baltimore with Patrick Ricard."

Cleveland already has Michael Burton at fullback, but they could certainly upgrade over the veteran. The Browns also lack depth at tight end behind Harold Fannin Jr., so adding a tight end could be huge.

Meanwhile, the Browns may not trade away players now that their season is going well. That could take players like Jerry Jeudy off the trade block.

"Because the team is winning, and because the Cleveland Browns are 5-2, so many of the trade conversations that I think a lot of people were talking about, maybe several weeks ago, have quieted," Ian Rapoport said on Monday via NFL Network. "Jerry Jeudy was the target of speculation in the rumor mill for a long time, actually going back to last year. It does not seem to me that the Cleveland Browns will now trade Jerry Jeudy, because they're good."

Cleveland is set to have 11 picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. It will be interesting to see how far they reach into their war chest, if at all, at the deadline.

articles.title: Blake Cashman Named NFC Defensive Player of the Week
articles.summary: It’s getting to be a routine
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings played a football game this past Sunday. And, because it's now Wednesday, that means it's time for one of their players to be recognized with a weekly award from the National Football League.

The league has just announced that Vikings' linebacker Blake Cashman has been named the NFC's Defensive Player of the Week for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season.

If it seemed like Cashman was all over the place in the Vikings' 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts this past Sunday, that's only because. . .well, he was. Cashman recorded 12 tackles on the afternoon, including eight solo tackles and two tackles for loss. He also had two quarterback sacks (a career high), three quarterback hits, and four passes defended. It was the twentieth game of his NFL career with at least ten tackles, and his sixteenth since joining the Vikings.

Sunday's game was also the seventeenth straight game where Cashman recorded at least seven tackles, which is the longest current streak in the NFL and the longest streak for a Viking dating back to at least 1987. He's the first player to have two sacks and four passes defended in a game since Alex Brown of the Chicago Bears did so in 2005, and the first player since at least 1982 (when the NFL first started recording sacks) to have at least twelve tackles, two sacks, and four passes defended in a game.

Seems like a pretty solid outing, all things considered.

We're now seven weeks into the season, and this is the fifth week where a member of the Vikings has been recognized with a weekly award. The only weeks where a Viking was not recognized were Week 1 when they defeated the Packers and Week 6 when they were on their bye week. Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers, return specialist Myles Price, and kicker Will Reichard were named NFC Special Teams Players of the Week in Weeks 2, 3, and 4, respectively (with Price being named the NFC's Special Teams Player of the Month for September for good measure), with cornerback Byron Murphy being recognized as the NFC's Defensive Player of the Week in Week 5.

Congratulations to Blake Cashman for being named the NFC's Defensive Player of the Week for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season!

articles.title: 'Football 301' on NFL trade deadline: Jags WR Brian Thomas Jr., Titans RB Tony Pollard and 4 other players to watch

articles.body:
As the NFL trade deadline approaches, speculation is ramping up about which players could be changing teams to reshape playoff races — or accelerate rebuilds. On a recent episode of Yahoo Sports' "Football 301" podcast, host Nate Tice and guest Gregg Rosenthal of the "NFL Daily" podcast offered their perspectives on top targets, ideal landing spots and what contending teams must consider before making a deal.

Here's a breakdown of players to watch, with a look at the ideas and analysis brought forward by Tice and Rosenthal.

Rosenthal highlighted BTJ as underutilized in Jacksonville, making him a prime trade deadline candidate. Thomas could unlock explosiveness for receiver-needy contenders like the Ravens or Chiefs, noting that his rookie contract increases his trade value.

The Rams were also mentioned as a potential "scheme fit" due to their need for speed, as they're currently "the most station-to-station offense in the league right now, which is crazy to think for a team quarterbacked by Matthew Stafford," Rosenthal said.

His ultimate landing spot for Thomas is Baltimore.

"How about let's just put BTJ, Zay Flowers and Lamar [Jackson] on the field together, and let's have some fun," Rosenthal said.

One concept discussed was sending Pollard to the Vikings, who need juice in their running game with Aaron Jones Sr. banged up (knee) and Jordan Mason underwhelming.

Tice noted Pollard's age (29) and expiring contract make him an attainable option for teams aiming to boost rushing production without a long-term commitment. Tice also weighed the trade dynamics of other backs (Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor), ultimately viewing Pollard as the easiest to pry away without getting into complicated negotiations.

"I still have optimism about the Vikings' offense, but they need guys, I think, on the ground that can just create some stuff just to boost their offensive line a little bit," Tice said.

Tice spotlighted Baker as a fit for the Bills, who have been gashed in the secondary and need a tone-setter in the middle of the field. Baker's versatility and aggression would mesh with Buffalo's scheme.

"Budda Baker can give them a guy that can play in the box, a guy that can run up and help both ways, pass and run, and also fit in [coordinator] Jim Leonard's defense."

Greenard was offered up as a candidate for the Chiefs, a team looking to add pass-rushing heat. Rosenthal acknowledged the contract hurdles (notably Greenard's guaranteed money), but argued Kansas City's defense could accommodate another edge presence for a stretch run.

Rosenthal called Ojomo "the prize" among Eagles defenders likely to be dangled, suggesting a match with the Jaguars. The move would inject quickness and interior disruption alongside DaVon Hamilton and help offset lackluster pass rush production.

Stewart emerged as another Bills candidate for Tice. He's a two-down space eater who could fortify Buffalo's run defense and allow the team's gap-shooters to roam freely. It's a low-cost, high-impact transaction at a position of need for contenders.
